thread:
incident-bot: Incident created (SEV-2) — tokenizer service high CPU leading to OOM kills across us-west2. Auto-detect: pod restarts > 5/min on tokenizer-replicaset.

marta: paging @channel — seeing a sustained tokenize loop spike. Multiple tokenizer pods (tokenizer-v4) hit cpu cgroup OOM on us-west2-a, causing kubelet to evict. 5+ restarts in 15m.

kevin: oncall here. initial notes: metrics show node cpu saturated, processes stuck in `tokenize_loop` for very long prompts. error logs from pod: ```
E 14:23:01 tokenizer.py:502 handle_request() - Uncaught exception: CPU OOM - cannot allocate thread stack
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/tokenizer.py", line 498, in handle_request
    tokens = tokenizer.batch_tokenize(requests)
  File "/app/tokenizer/core.py", line 221, in batch_tokenize
    while True: # heavy prompt loop
MemoryError: failed to allocate
```

olivia: adding logs from node `ip-10-0-4-12`: ```
Out of memory: Kill process 23456 (python3) score 987 or sacrifice child
Killed process 23456 (python3) total-vm:204800000kB, anon-rss:198000000kB, file-rss:0kB
```

carlos: noticed CUDA errors on adjacent gpu nodes too around same time: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` — likely unrelated but bumped by same workload. GPU jobs showing sporadic kernel failures shortly after CPU OOMs on prep side.

amy: customer impact: error rate for /v1/generate up from 0.8% -> 11% for customers hitting large prompt route. Incident ticket INC-2026 created and customer support notified. Major customers A and C seeing increased latency/timeouts.

marta: immediate mitigation steps I'm pushing now: 1) scale tokenizer replicas down to reduce pressure on nodes for short term, 2) apply temporary route-level circuit breaker to direct heavy prompt routes to fallback smaller tokenizer (tokenizer-lite), 3) patch ConfigMap to limit max concurrent tokenization threads per pod.

deploy-bot: Triggered patch: `kubectl set env deployment/tokenizer-v4 MAX_WORKERS=2 --namespace=prod` — rollout started.

kevin: running quick one-off to drain nodes with worst OOMs: ```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-4-12 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-4-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n prod```
Applied to ip-10-0-4-12 and ip-10-0-4-14. This will cause some pods to reschedule to less loaded nodes.

olivia: also adding an emergency autoscaler tweak: reduce `targetConcurrency` for tokenizer-service HPA from 80 -> 40 to avoid building up queue length. patch applied.

carlos: rolling restart of tokenizer-v4 to pick up MAX_WORKERS=2 env var. watching for backoff: no crashloop yet.

marta: running a temporary routing rule in API gateway to divert `route: /v1/generate` requests with prompt_length > 40k to `tokenizer-lite` until we have a better fix. Config change: ```
- condition: request.header.prompt-length > 40000
  action: route->tokenizer-lite
```

amy: Customer impact update: error rate down to ~3.4% after diversion and scale changes. Latency for heavy prompts increased but not failing. Support updated SLAs and emailed top 10 customers.

kevin: root cause hypothesis: a small percentage (~0.6%) of incoming prompts are extremely long with repeated patterns causing the tokenizer to hit pathological backtracking in regex-based tokenization, which grows memory unexpectedly and spawns many threads. Patch candidate in branch `fix/tokenizer-backtrack-limit` adds a protective cutoff and switches heavy requests to stream-based tokenizer.

marta: can we hotfix the running image without full deploy? suggestion: mount ephemeral configmap with `TOKENIZE_MAX_STEPS=2000` which forces early bailout.

kevin: applied configmap `tokenizer-safety-2367` and toggled feature flag `tokenizer_bailout=true`. Verified pods reloaded config via SIGHUP proxy. logs show bailout triggers now for heavy prompts: ```
bailout: prompt too long, falling back to streaming mode, request_id=abc123
```

olivia: monitoring: node CPU pressure falling from 98% -> 62% over 12m. pod restarts reduced to 0-1/min. GPU errors persisted for a bit but stopped after node drains.

carlos: filed PR to add non-backtracking tokenization algorithm and a safelist for customers that legitimately need very large prompts (we'll bat-case). PR #: 8791.

marta: escalation checklist: 1) Pager duty on-call loop closed for now, 2) SEs to reach out to customers flagged in INC-2026, 3) follow-up postmortem scheduled.

amy: temporary customer-facing notes drafted: "We observed increased error rates for requests with very large prompts. We have applied routing and config changes to stabilize service. Engineering is working on permanent fix."

kevin: handing off to night oncall @olivia — all mitigations are in place (MAX_WORKERS=2, tokenizer_bailout=true, route diversion, node drains). watchlist: error rate, pod restart, node oom. If it reoccurs, escalate to eng-runtime and consider pausing heavy-prompt route entirely.

olivia: acknowledged, will monitor metrics and alerts. leaving playbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tokenizer-hotloop and incident ticket INC-2026.

marta: post-incident action items (short): - revert MAX_WORKERS after PR validated, - ship non-backtracking tokenizer with canary, - add surge protection quota per org to prevent single-customer blast, - improve alerting to detect regex backtracking patterns earlier.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 closed to SEV-2 status -> mitigated.

kevin: final note before sleep: good collaboration. please add any missed notes to the ticket. handing off monitoring to olivia.

olivia: 10-4, will update if things change. :thumbsup:
